one_month_reasoning: The target date 2026-11-01 is a Sunday, so the relevant close is Friday 2026-10-30. Lattice's own Q3 report is scheduled for 2026-11-03, after the window, so its main scheduled catalyst falls outside it. Events inside the window are read-throughs from the value chain: TSMC's mid-October results, Aspeed's September monthly revenue (around 10 October; ten straight monthly records through August, +118% y/y), and late-October hyperscaler earnings with capex guidance (MSFT/GOOGL/META/AMZN). These have mostly been positive, but they are well known and mostly priced in. Pre-earnings positioning into a guide that already beat consensus by about 32% gives a slight upward tilt, which is offset by the stock sitting about 15% below its $157 high after a +82% year. I used a near-symmetric lognormal centred at $134.5 with monthly sigma of about 17% (61% / 3.5).

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (35x on an estimated CY2028 EPS of $3.95 = $138, weight 0.6) and EV/NTM sales (12x on about $1.45B of NTM revenue at Oct-2027, minus about $0.7B net debt, over 143M shares = $117, weight 0.4), which gives about $130.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: CY2028E EPS $3.95 x 35x (the NTM multiple the market would apply in Oct-2027)

inputs_detail.derivation: 2027 consensus $3.21 grown about 23%. That is below the 2026-27 pace (+50%) because AI-server unit growth is set to slow (TrendForce sees CSP capex growth easing from ~90% in 2026 to ~50% in 2027), while BMC peer Aspeed's demand stays very strong.

LSCC's historical mean P/E is about 49x (TIKR), and today it trades at about 42x 2027 consensus ($134 / $3.21). I apply a discount because AMI adds debt and a lower-growth software mix, and because cyclical semi peers (MCHP, AMD embedded) are early in recovery and trade at lower multiples.

inputs_detail.derivation: The FPGA run rate of about $880M/yr (Q3 guide midpoint x4) grows about 25-30% as AI-server attach continues and industrial recovers: Arrow's book-to-bill is above 1 with backlog into 1H27, and Microchip is up 38% y/y. Add AMI at about $240M/yr growing about 10%.
Today's EV is about $19.8B ($134 x 142.0M shares plus ~$0.8B net debt), about 16x 2027E sales. I compress to 12x NTM as growth decelerates from the 2026 acquisition-plus-recovery spike.

$925M term loan drawn on 2026-07-27, against $173M cash at 2026-07-04 less the cash part of the deal. That gives about $0.8B net debt now, falling to about $0.7B after roughly $300M/yr of FCF (Q2 non-GAAP FCF $81M) less amortisation and buybacks.

bear.story: AI-server build pauses or digests in 2027 (capex growth slows faster than TrendForce's ~50%), and FPGA attach in AI racks normalises. Industrial recovery stalls once distributors' restocking ends, and AMI integration and leverage weigh on the stock. EPS of about $2.7 at 28x.

base.story: FPGA grows about 25% on server and comms plus a steady industrial recovery, AMI performs to plan, and 2028E EPS is about $3.9. The multiple compresses to about 35x, so the stock goes roughly sideways to modestly up.

bull.story: AI-server and custom-ASIC racks keep up 30%+ unit growth into 2027. Lattice gains control-FPGA share and cross-sells AMI BMC/BIOS to hyperscalers, revenue runs above $1.6B, EPS is about $4.8, and the premium multiple holds at about 45x.

thesis_break_reason: A drop to about $85 (-37%, below the post-AMI-announcement range and about 26x 2027 consensus) would most likely mean that AI-server/hyperscaler demand (the 63% Compute & Communications segment) has rolled over, or that AMI has lost BMC/BIOS share, rather than just a multiple swing. Value-chain checks to watch: Aspeed's monthly revenue turning negative y/y, hyperscaler capex cuts, or distributor book-to-bill falling below 1.

reasoning: Company facts: Q2-26 revenue was $201M (+62% y/y), Compute & Communications +83% to 63% of revenue, and non-GAAP EPS $0.53. The Q3 guide of $245-265M includes two months of AMI ($1.65B deal: $925M term loan plus about 5.2M shares). Value-chain evidence is uniformly strong. Aspeed (70-80% server BMC share) has posted ten straight monthly revenue records (Aug +118% y/y). TrendForce raised its 2026 AI-server growth forecast to ~31% and sees 9-CSP capex of about $887B in 2026 and $1.3T in 2027 (+50%). AMD embedded grew +19% y/y in Q2 (best in 3 years), Altera is guiding +25% for 2026, Microchip is +38% y/y with channel inventory at 25 days, and Arrow reports book-to-bill above 1 in all regions with backlog into 1H27. So the industry backs both the AI-server and the industrial legs into 2027. The offset is valuation: about 42x 2027 consensus EPS of $3.21 and about 16x EV/sales, with the cycle likely past peak growth rates by late 2027. Fair value of about $130 is close to spot, while momentum and consensus targets (avg ~$165) skew upside. I set the 12-month median at about $136 with a lognormal sigma of 0.53 (below the 61% realized, since part of that came from the AMI and earnings spikes, but still high for a richly valued AI-linked semi), giving P(>=134) of about 0.51. Scenarios are 25/50/25 at $75/$135/$215 (probability-weighted about $140), consistent with the ladder. Research was limited to about 15 queries; X/social sources were not used.
